newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai immigration detains Cambodia's Sam Rainsy.
newsitem.headline: Thai immigration detains Cambodia's Sam Rainsy.

text.p: Thai immigration officials detained Cambodian opposition leader Sam Rainsy on Wednesday as he tried to enter Cambodia's Poipet town, witnesses said.

Sam Rainsy went to Poipet, a town on Cambodia's western border controlled by royalist forces loyal to ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, on Tuesday to meet members of his Khmer Nation Party who had fled Phnom Penh fearing repression from Second Prime Minister Hun Sen. Hun Sen took control of the government earlier this month.
Thai officials at Aranyaprathet, a town on the Thai side of the border, said Sam Rainsy's trip to Poipet on Tuesday had been illegal.

A Thai army officer told Reuters that Sam Rainsy had caused trouble for Thailand by using Thai soil as a base for a campaign against Hun Sen. The opposition leader had called for resistance against Hun Sen, who violently ousted royalist forces from Phnom Penh.
"He has caused trouble for Thailand and has used Thai soil to wage a campaign against the Cambodian government," the officer said.

Sam Rainsy said on Tuesday that he had met the deposed Ranariddh in France and had agreed to join the prince's FUNCINPEC party to resist Hun Sen's takeover of the Cambodian government through what he called illegal means.
